name: City Council Meeting - Jun 18, 2024
agenda_text:
TORRANCE CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
  JUNE 18, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING
  5:00 P.M. - CLOSED SESSION
  6:30 P.M. - REGULAR BUSINESS BEGINS
  IN COUNCIL CHAMBER AT 3031 TORRANCE BL.

  CITY COUNCIL MAY TAKE ACTION ON ANY ITEM LISTED ON THE AGENDA

City Council 06-18-24

OPENING CEREMONIES

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  ROLL CALL
  : Councilmembers Gerson, Kaji, Kalani, Lewis, Mattucci, Sheikh, and Mayor Chen

14.  CLOSED SESSION

  14A. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION (California
  Government Code §54956.9(d)(1)):
  1)  City of Whittier v. Superior Court of the State of California County of Los Angeles, et al.
  LASC Case No. 23STCP03579
  2)  Blake Williams v. Eve Berg, et al. LASC Case No. 21TRCV00034
  14A - STAFF REPORT

  14B. PUBLIC EMPLOYEE DISCIPLINE/DISMISSAL/RELEASE  (California
  Government Code §54957)

  14C. PUBLIC EMPLOYEE DISCIPLINE/DISMISSAL/RELEASE  (California

  14D. PUBLIC EMPLOYEE DISCIPLINE/DISMISSAL/RELEASE  (California
  Government Code §54957)

  14E. REAL PROPERTY – CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR
  (California Government Code §54956.8):
  1)  Property: Hawthorne Boulevard from Pacific Coast Highway to north City limit Agency
  Negotiator: Aram Chaparyan Negotiating Parties: City of Torrance and California
  Department of Transportation (Caltrans) Under Negotiation: Price and terms and
  conditions of relinquishment

  14F. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR (California Government Code
  §54957.6): Agency Negotiator: Aram Chaparyan Employee
  Organization/Association:
  1. Certain Full-Time Salaried and Hourly Employees
  2. Certain Part-Time Hourly Employees
  3. Crossing Guards

  5. Engineers and Torrance Fiscal Employees Association
  6. Executive & Management Employees
  7. Police & Fire Trainees

  10. Fire Safety Management
  11. Torrance Fire Fighters Association
  12. Torrance Library Employees Association
   13. Torrance Municipal Employees/AFSCME Local 1117 AFL-CIO
  14. Torrance Police Commanders Association (TPCA)
  15. Torrance Police Officers Association
  16. Torrance Professional Parks & Recreation Employees Organization
  17. Torrance Professional & Supervisory Association
  18. Torrance Recurrent Recreational Employees Organization
  19. City Treasurer
  20. City Attorney

10A. City Manager - Conduct Closed Hearing on the Appeal of the Civil Service
  Commission Decision Sustaining the Termination of a Police Officer (6). Confidential
  under Penal Code 832.7 and Copley Press v. Superior Court 39 Cal. 4th 1272 (2006).
  Consideration of public employee discipline will be conducted in closed session per
  California Government Code Section 54957(b)(1), unless the employee requests to
  have the appeal conducted in public session. The deliberation of this matter by the
  City Council will occur in closed session. Expenditure: None.
  10A - STAFF REPORT

RECESSED TO CLOSED SESSION

10A. City Manager - Conduct Closed Hearing on the Appeal of the Civil Service
  Commission Decision Sustaining the Termination of a Police Officer (6). Confidential
  under Penal Code 832.7 and Copley Press v. Superior Court 39 Cal. 4th 1272 (2006).
  Consideration of public employee discipline will be conducted in closed session per
  California Government Code Section 54957(b)(1), unless the employee requests to
  have the appeal conducted in public session. The deliberation of this matter by the
  City Council will occur in closed session. Expenditure: None.

CONCLUDE CLOSED SESSION RECESS

RECONVENED IN PUBLIC SESSION

2.  FLAG SALUTE: Councilmember Mattucci NON-SECTARIAN INVOCATION:
  Councilmember Sheikh

3.  REPORT OF THE CITY CLERK ON THE POSTING OF THE AGENDA The agenda was
  posted on the Public Notice Board at 3031 Torrance Bl. and on the City’s Website on
  Wednesday, June 12, 2024 /s/ Rebecca Poirier
  3 - AFFIDAVIT

MOTION TO WAIVE FURTHER READING OF RESOLUTIONS AND ORDINANCES AFTER
NUMBER & TITLE – See Council Rules of Order Section 2.11 (Resolution 2006-65)

4.  ANNOUNCEMENT OF WITHDRAWN, DEFERRED, AND/OR SUPPLEMENTAL ITEMS

5.  COUNCIL COMMITTEE MEETINGS AND ANNOUNCEMENTS

6.  COMMUNITY MATTERS – None Scheduled.

7.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS #1 (Limited up to a 15-minute period) This portion of the
  meeting is reserved for comments on items under the Consent Calendar or items that
  are not on the agenda. Under the Ralph M. Brown Act, City Council cannot act on
  items raised during public comment, but may respond briefly to statements made or
  questions posed; request clarification; or refer the item to staff. Speakers under Orals
  are limited to either Oral Communications #1 or Oral Communications #2 and no
  longer than 1 minute per speaker. Time starts when you step up to the microphone. If
  presenting handout material to Council, please provide 11 copies to the City Clerk
  before speaking. Handouts will be distributed while you speak.
  PUBLIC COMMENT
  PUBLIC COMMENT RECIEVED AFTER 5:30 P.M. ON 6/17/24 AND BEFORE 11:11 P.M. ON
  6/18/24/24
 8.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  Matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion and one
  vote. There will be no separate discussion of these items. If discussion is desired, that item will be removed by
  a Councilmember from the Consent Calendar and considered separately..

  8A. City Manager – Approve Request to Set Closed Hearing Date to Consider
  Employee Termination Appeal. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council approve request to set a date of
  Tuesday, August 13, 2024 to conduct a closed hearing to consider an appeal of the Civil
  Service Commission’s decision sustaining the termination of a Police Officer (8).
  8A - STAFF REPORT

  8B. City Treasurer - Accept and File Investment Report for the Month of April 2024.
  Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Treasurer that City Council accept and file the Investment
  Report for the month of April 2024.
  8B - STAFF REPORT

  8C. Community Development – Approve Third Amendment to Consulting Services
  Agreement for Seismic Retrofit Ordinance Implementation. Expenditure: $40,000
  (General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Community Development Director that City Council approve a third
  amendment to the consulting services agreement with Degenkolb Engineers of Los
  Angeles, CA (C2021-019) in the amount of $40,000, for a new not-to-exceed amount of
  $464,770, to provide implementation services for a seismic retrofit ordinance, and to extend
  the contract term for an additional one-year period beginning July 1, 2024 and ending June
  30, 2025.
  8C - STAFF REPORT
  8C - SUPPLEMENTAL #1
  8C - SUPPLEMENTAL #2

  8D. Community Services – Approve Conceptual Float Design for 2025 Pasadena
  Tournament of Roses Parade. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Community Services Director that City Council approve the
  conceptual float design as the City's float entry in the Pasadena Tournament of Roses
  Parade on January 1, 2025.
  8D - STAFF REPORT
  8D - STAFF PRESENTATION

  8E.  Community Services - Approve City-County Municipal Services Agreement for
  Sole Source Animal Care and Control Services. Expenditure: Not-to-Exceed
  $1,600,000 (General Fund: Approximately $320,000 Annually).
  Recommendation of the Community Services Director that City Council approve a City-
  County municipal services agreement with the County of Los Angeles Department of
  Animal Care and Control for an amount not-to-exceed $1,600,000 to provide sole
  source animal care and control services for a five-year period beginning July 1, 2024
  and ending June 30, 2029.
  8E - STAFF REPORT

  8F.  Finance – Approve Policy Renewal for Property Insurance Coverage and
  Authorize the Finance Director to Execute the Policy. Expenditure: Not-to-Exceed
  $683,925.34 (Non-General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Finance Director that City Council:
  1) Approve the policy renewal for property insurance coverage with the Alliant Property
  Insurance Program (APIP) through Alliant Insurance Services, Inc. of Irvine, CA for an
  amount not-to-exceed $683,925.34 plus taxes and fees for a one-year period beginning
  July 1, 2024 and ending July 1, 2025; and
  2) Authorize the Finance Director or designee to execute the insurance policy.
  8F- STAFF REPORT

  8G. Finance – Approve Policy Renewal for Excess Workers’ Compensation Insurance
  Coverage and Authorize the Finance Director to Execute the Policy. Expenditure:
  Not-to-Exceed $457,000 (Non-General Fund).
   Recommendation of the Finance Director that City Council:
  1) Approve the policy renewal for excess workers’ compensation insurance coverage with
  Public Risk Innovation, Solutions, and Management (PRISM) through Alliant Insurance
  Services, Inc. of Irvine, CA for an amount not-to-exceed $457,000 for a one-year period
  beginning July 1, 2024 and ending July 1, 2025; and
  2) Authorize the Finance Director or designee to execute the insurance policy.
  8G - STAFF REPORT

  8H. Finance – Approve Policy Renewal for Automobile Physical Damage Insurance
  Coverage and Authorize the Finance Director to Execute the Policy. Expenditure:
  Not-to-Exceed $400,000 (Non-General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Finance Director that City Council:
  1) Approve the policy renewal for automobile physical damage insurance coverage with
  The Hanover Insurance Group, Inc. through Alliant Insurance Services, Inc. of Irvine,
  CA for an amount not-to-exceed $400,000 plus taxes and fees for a one-year period
  beginning July 1, 2024 and ending July 1, 2025; and
  2) Authorize the Finance Director or designee to execute the policy.
  8H - STAFF REPORT

  8I.  City Manager - Approve Side Letter Agreements Between Torrance Police
  Officers Association (TPOA) and Management and Torrance Police Commanders
  Association (TPCA) and Management, and Torrance Professional and
  Supervisory Association (TPSA) and Management. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council:
  1) Approve a side letter agreement between the Torrance Police Officers Association
  (TPOA) and Management amending language pertaining to longevity steps and pay
  ranges; and
  2) Approve a side letter agreement between the Torrance Police Commanders
  Association (TPCA) and Management updating language pertaining to merit pay; and
  3) Approve a side letter agreement between the Torrance Professional and Supervisory
  Association (TPSA) and Management modifying the pay range for the Transit Training
  Coordinator classification.
  8I - STAFF REPORT
  8I - MATERIAL AVAILABLE

10.  HEARINGS

  10C. Community Development – Consider Appeal of Planning Commission Adoption
  of a Mitigated Negative Declaration and Approval of a General Plan Amendment
  to Amend the Land Use Designation from General Commercial (C-GEN) to
  Medium High Density Residential (R-MH), in Conjunction with a Conditional Use
  Permit to Allow the Construction of a 272-Unit Residential Condominium
  Development with a Density Bonus, a Planned Development to Establish
  Development Standards for the Development Plan, and a Division of Lot to Allow
  a Vesting Tentative Tract Map for Condominium Purposes, on Property Located
  in the P-D Zone at 2325 Crenshaw Boulevard (APN 7359-028-233), Herein
  Referred as the Torrance Del Amo Project. The Potential Environmental Impacts
  Associated with the Project have been Assessed in an Initial Study in
  Accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act. EAS23-00005, GPA23-
  00002, CUP23-00027, PUD23-00001, DIV23-00008: ROSE EQUITIES (OPTIMUS
  PROPERTIES, LLC). Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Planning Commission and the Community Development Director
  that City Council:
  1) Deny the appeal; and
  2) Adopt a RESOLUTION adopting a Mitigated Negative Declaration for the Torrance Del
  Amo Project in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act; and
  3) Adopt a RESOLUTION approving a General Plan Amendment as provided for in
  Division 9, Chapter 2, Article 34 of the Torrance Municipal Code to allow an amendment
  to the Land Use designation from General Commercial to Medium High Density
  Residential on property located in the P-D Zone at 2325 Crenshaw Boulevard (APN
  7359-028-233); and
  4) Adopt a RESOLUTION approving a Conditional Use Permit as provided for in Division
  9, Chapter 5, Article 1 of the Torrance Municipal Code to allow the construction of a
  272-unit residential condominium development with density bonus on property located
   in the P-D Zone at 2325 Crenshaw Boulevard (APN 7359-028-233); and
  5)  Adopt a RESOLUTION approving a Planned Development as provided for in Division 9
  Chapter 1, Article 42 of the Torrance Municipal Code to establish development
  standards for a development plan for property located in the P-D Zone at 2325
  Crenshaw Boulevard (APN 7359-028-233); and
  6)  Adopt a RESOLUTION approving a Division of Lot as provided for in Division 9 Chapter
  2, Article 29 of the Torrance Municipal Code to allow a Vesting Tentative Tract Map for
  condominium purposes on property located in the P-D Zone at 2325 Crenshaw
  Boulevard (APN 7359-028-233).
  10C - STAFF REPORT PART 1
  10C - STAFF REPORT PART 2
  10C - STAFF REPORT PART 3
  10C - SUPPLEMENTAL
  10C - STAFF PRESENTATION
  10C - APPLICANT PRESENTATION

RECESS

RECONVENE

10B. Public Works – Conduct Public Hearing and Adopt RESOLUTION Confirming a
  Diagram and Assessment for Fiscal Year 2024-25 in Connection with City of Torrance
  Lighting District No. 99-1. Expenditure: $1,866,272 (General Fund and Non-General
  Funds)

  1)  Conduct a public hearing on the proposed levy of assessments within the City of
  Torrance Lighting District No. 99-1 for fiscal year 2024-25; and

  2)  Adopt a RESOLUTION confirming a diagram and assessment for fiscal year
  2024-25 in connection with the City of Torrance Lighting District No. 99-1.
  10B - STAFF REPORT

9.  ADMINISTRATIVE MATTERS

  9A. Finance – Approve Program Modification in the Community Services
  Department’s Fiscal Year 2024-25 Operating Budget. Expenditure: $29,203
  Annually (General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Finance Director that City Council approve a program modification
  to add a 0.5 full-time equivalent Maintenance Worker position in the Community Services
  Department’s fiscal year 2024-25 operating budget in the amount of $29,203 per year.
  9A - STAFF REPORT

  9B. City Manager and Community Services – Award Contract Services Agreement for
  Unarmed Security Guard Services. Expenditure: Not-to-Exceed $546,415.44
  (General Fund).
  Recommendation of the City Manager and Community Services Director that City Council
  award a contract services agreement to Citiguard, Inc. of West Hills, CA (RFP B2024-04) for
  an amount not-to-exceed $546,415.44 to provide unarmed security guard services at City
  Hall, LeRoy J. Jackson Council Chamber, Katy Geissert Civic Center Library, and the
  Torrance Farmers’ Market for a three-year period beginning July 1, 2024 and ending June
  30, 2027.
  9B - STAFF REPORT PART 1
  9B - STAFF REPORT PART 2
  9B - STAFF REPORT PART 3

  9C. Public Works – Adopt RESOLUTION Adopting a List of Projects for Fiscal Year
  2024-25 as Funded by SB 1: The Road Repair and Accountability Act and
  Appropriate Funds. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the Public Works Director that City Council:
  1) Adopt a RESOLUTION adopting a list of projects for fiscal year 2024-25 as funded by
  SB 1: The Road Repair and Accountability Act to identify the Residential Pavement
  Improvement, I-159 as the project to be funded; and
  2) Appropriate Road Maintenance and Rehabilitation Account (RMRA) funds in the
   amount of $353,686 to the Residential Pavement Improvement, I-159; and
  3)  Appropriate additional prior fiscal years’ RMRA revenues received from the State of
  California in the amount of $575,000 to the Residential Pavement Improvement, I-159.
  9C - STAFF REPORT

  9D. Public Works – Authorize Sole-Source Purchase Order for Neptune Advanced
  Metering Infrastructure Water Meter Registers. Expenditure: Not-to-Exceed
  $6,500,000 (Non-General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Public Works Director that City Council authorize a sole-source
  purchase order with Ferguson Waterworks of Poway, CA for an amount not-to-exceed
  $6,500,000 for 26,500 Neptune Advanced Metering Infrastructure water meter registers.
  9D - STAFF REPORT

  9E.  Finance – Approve Policy Renewal for Excess Liability Insurance Coverage and
  Authorize the Finance Director to Execute the Policy. Expenditure: Not-to-Exceed
  $3,957,200 (Non-General Fund).
  Recommendation of the Finance Director that City Council:
  1) Approve the policy renewal for excess liability insurance coverage with Public Risk
  Innovation, Solutions, and Management (PRISM) through Alliant Insurance Services,
  Inc. of Irvine, CA for an amount not-to-exceed $3,957,200 for a one-year period
  beginning July 1, 2024 and ending July 1, 2025; and
  2) Authorize the Finance Director or designee to execute the insurance policy.
  9E - STAFF REPORT

  9F.  City Manager – Approve Third Amendment to Amended and Restated Lease with
  South End Racquet and Health Club, Inc. for City-Owned Property Located at
  2800 Skypark Drive. Expenditure: None.
  Recommendation of the City Manager that City Council approve a third Amendment to the
  amended and restated lease with the South End Racquet and Health Club, Inc. of Torrance,
  CA (C-1990) for City-owned property located at 2800 Skypark Drive, to consolidate the
  original lease into one comprehensive document and set forth certain agreements
  concerning the second Fair Market Valuation Period effective July 1, 2024.
  9F - STAFF REPORT

  9G. City Attorney – Approve Third Amendment to Fee Agreement for Legal Services.
  Expenditure: $70,000 (General Fund).
  Recommendation of the City Attorney that City Council approve a third amendment to the
  fee agreement with law firm Liebert Cassidy Whitmore of Los Angeles (C2023-115) in the
  amount of $70,000, for a new not-to-exceed amount of $320,000, to provide the City with
  legal services pertaining to Civil Service Appeal Matter #A23-000790.
  9G - STAFF REPORT

11.  AGENCY AGENDAS

12.  2ND READING ORDINANCES – None Scheduled.

13.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS #2 (Limited up to a 15-minute period) This portion of the
  meeting is reserved for comments on items not on the agenda. Under the Ralph M.
  Brown Act, City Council cannot act on items raised during public comment, but may
  respond briefly to statements made or questions posed; request clarification; or refer
  the item to staff. Speakers under Orals are limited to either Oral Communications #1
  or Oral Communications #2 and no longer than 1 minute per speaker. Time starts
  when you step up to the microphone. If presenting handout material to Council,
  please provide 11 copies to the City Clerk before speaking. Handouts will be
  distributed while you speak.

  Council Order - Sheikh, Gerson, Kaji, Kalani, Lewis, Mattucci, Mayor Chen

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION

15.  ADJOURNMENT
 15A. Adjournment of the City Council meeting to Tuesday, July 2, 2024, at 5:00 p.m.
  for closed session, with regular business commencing at 6:30 p.m. in the Toyota
  Meeting Hall. Tuesday, June 25, 2024, is a Council Dark Night.
  15A - STAFF REPORT
